text: A task force set up to raise funding for railway projects
HÀ NỘI - The Ministry of Finance has established a 30-member task force to study and develop mechanisms to raise funding for high-speed and urban railway development.

Under the decision signed by Minister of Finance Ngô Văn Tuấn, Deputy Minister Tạ Anh Tuấn was appointed as head of the task force and Lê Thành Quân, director of the ministry's Department of Investment and Infrastructure Development, as standing deputy head.

Aother members come from various units under the Ministry of Finance and relevant ministries, central agencies and local authorities, including the Ministry of Construction, the Ministry of Justice, the State Bank of Vietnam, the Hà Nội and HCM City people's committees, and Vietnam Railways Corporation.

The task force is responsible for researching and developing a proposal on mechanisms and policies to mobilise resources for high-speed and urban railway projects, and submitting it to the Prime Minister for consideration and approval.
The move comes as Việt Nam faces substantial investment requirements to expand its railway infrastructure, while state budget resources remain constrained.

The North-South high-speed railway project alone has received in-principle approval from the National Assembly, with preliminary total investment estimated at more than VNĐ1.7 quadrillion (US$66.25 billion).
Meanwhile, urban railway development in Hà Nội and HCM City continues to face challenges related to funding and implementation progress.
Railway projects typically involve long payback periods, modest financial returns and substantial risks, which limit their appeal to private investors.

Other potential funding sources, including revenue from land development, transit-oriented development (TOD) and the commercial exploitation of railway infrastructure assets, have yet to be fully tapped.
Beyond infrastructure construction, railway development also requires substantial resources for the domestic railway industry, technology transfer and the training of a highly skilled workforce.
The proposed funding framework is expected to address these requirements and identify mechanisms to diversify investment sources for Việt Nam's railway development. - VNS
